Hi Kim — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: Calendly/Chili Piper sometimes fall back to a server-side or account locale instead of using the browser locale, which causes the widget to show PST for some customers. Two quick workarounds that have worked for APAC customers:

1) Open the link with an explicit timezone parameter — e.g. https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?tz=Asia%2FTokyo — that forces the widget to render in the correct TZ.

2) If that still looks off, accept the draft and use the ICS we attach; the ICS contains an explicit TZID so calendar apps will place the event correctly. I've attached a quick ICS (demo-invite.ics) with the 10:00 JST slot as a concrete option. If you prefer 14:00 JST I can update and re-send.

We're also going to add a small rule to our Chili Piper config to append the tz param for APAC-listed emails (Marissa is looping in infra to track).

Attachment: demo-invite.ics (text/calendar)

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Kim — looping in to confirm and tidy up the invites.

Short answer: the ICS I just attached (demo-invite-tz-fixed.ics) is the canonical invite and has TZID=Asia/Tokyo on all DTSTART/DTEND properties. Please delete the Calendly-created duplicate in your calendar and accept the attached one; that will ensure everyone (Tokyo, Sydney, and our side) sees the same absolute clock time.

Why duplicates happen: Calendly will sometimes send an email invite and also create an event via its API. If account-level TZ detection is wrong, those two sources can differ. We're putting a guard in Chili Piper to add ?tz for APAC emails and to suppress the auto-API event when an ICS has been accepted.
